dashboard.label: Webex Bot Alerts
dashboard.description: Send Splunk / ITSI alerts to your Webex space, and run the live break-it demo.

div.div: The Webex message is sent by the Alerts app (not ITSI). Set up a bot once, then trigger it by breaking something in the lab.
1. Enable the alert once — Settings ▸ Searches, reports, and alerts → turn on “dcloud - Incident: services degraded → Webex episode”.
2. Break something — on the Proxmox host (198.18.3.11, as root):
(Or on the Splunk box, where the repo lives — it SSHes to Proxmox: bash /opt/dcloud-splunk/ubuntu/demo-chaos.sh break-web)
3. Watch: a Webex message arrives (status below turns green), Correlation ▸ Service Glass Table goes red, and ITSI ▸ Service Analyzer cascades.
Alerts run every 5 min — for a live audience set the alert’s cron to * * * * * to fire within a minute.

search.query: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd "webex_notify:" | rex field=_raw "webex_notify:\s+(?<detail>.*)$" | eval Result=case(like(detail,"sent%"),"● sent", like(detail,"no Webex credential%"),"● no credential", 1==1,"● error") | table _time Result detail | sort - _time
| rest /servicesNS/-/alerts/saved/searches | search action.webex_notify=1 | eval Enabled=if(disabled=0 AND is_scheduled=1,"● on","○ off") | rename title as Alert | table Alert Enabled | sort Alert

html.div:
1. Bot token — at developer.webex.com create a bot and copy its Bot Access Token (the long ~108-char one — not the Bot ID).
2. Room — create a Webex space, add your bot to it, then get the space id from List Rooms (authenticated with the bot token).
3. Save it on the Splunk box (out-of-repo; read on every alert):
html.pre: sudo install -d -m750 -o splunk -g splunk /opt/splunk/var/lib/dcloud sudo -u splunk tee /opt/splunk/var/lib/dcloud/webex.env >/dev/null <<'EOF' WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN=<bot access token> WEBEX_ROOM_ID=<room id> EOF sudo chmod 600 /opt/splunk/var/lib/dcloud/webex.env
html.div: Simpler option: an incoming webhook — put WEBEX_WEBHOOK_URL=… in that file instead. Test without waiting for an alert:
html.pre: echo '{"search_name":"test","configuration":{"message":"✅ Webex wired up"}}' \ | sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk cmd python3 \ /opt/splunk/etc/apps/alerts/bin/webex_notify.py --execute

html.div:
Status meanings (table above): no credential → webex.env missing/empty · error → bot not in the space, bad token, or wrong room id (the detail column shows the HTTP code from Webex). Needs outbound HTTPS to webexapis.com.
Hand the lab to someone else / disconnect — nothing about your Webex is in the repo; remove the credential and the action simply no-ops until a new one is added:
For real ITSI Episodes (Episode Review + aggregation policy that sends Webex), build a Correlation Search + Notable Event Aggregation Policy in the ITSI UI — see the README “ITSI Episodes” section.
